title: Inspector verify_map
description: Per-element provenance map for the Inspector panel / coding-verifier layer. A FLAT object keyed by atomic element id; the values declare, for every claim/figure/media element on the page, exactly what backs it. The Inspector drawer renders one entry per id. See _doc.

_toc._comment: Navigation aid only — a non-validating annotation (JSON Schema ignores unknown keywords). The contract is unchanged; this just maps where each part of the schema lives.
_toc.properties._doc: Optional human-readable contract notes (purpose, id_prefixes, kind_selects_renderer, gallery_convention, byte_identity). Recommended as the first key of verify_map.json.
_toc.patternProperties.^(ana|det|des|sct|cin|: The per-element entry shape — one object per atomic id; its `kind` selects the drawer renderer.
_toc.$defs.computation: kind=computation — claim + code_file/code_lines + data_preview + expected_output + the runnable Run panel.
_toc.$defs.media: kind=media — real fetched asset + source_url + license + author + identity (+ gallery via flags||assets||photos).
_toc.$defs.generated: kind=generated — AI-asset preview + tool/model/prompt/disclosure + the real_default publish-safe fallback.
_toc.$defs.fact: kind=fact (and the credits variant) — claim + categorised sources[] each with its own facts[].
_toc.$defs.galleryItem: One gallery cell — its own source_url + license so attribution survives per asset.
_toc.$defs.codeLines: The [start,end] line-range shape used by computation.code_lines.
_toc.$defs.dataPreview: The curated input-rows preview shape shown above the Run panel.

_doc.description: Human-readable contract notes. Optional but recommended as the first key.

purpose.const: verify_map.json is the per-element provenance map the Inspector panel reads. Each non-underscore key is an ATOMIC element id that also appears as a data-* attribute in index.html. Clicking that element opens the Inspector drawer, which renders this entry.

id_prefixes.const: Keys are atomic ids namespaced by producing role: ana_* (analyst computation/finding), det_* (detective fact), des_* (designer element — may resolve to a computation, media, or generated kind), sct_* (scout-verified media), cin_* (cinematographer background imagery). A des_* element with no own analysis resolves through its data-ana/data-det binding.

kind_selects_renderer.const: The `kind` field selects which drawer renderer is used: 'computation' -> code + data_preview + expected_output + run panel (optionally a client-side reduced-N rerun); 'media' -> asset preview + source_url + license + identity provenance; 'generated' -> AI-asset preview + tool/model/prompt/disclosure + the real_default fallback; 'fact' -> claim + categorised sources[] with per-source facts[]; 'credits' -> the same fact renderer with a 'Credits' badge (a license/source aggregator).

gallery_convention.const: A multi-asset element carries a gallery array under one of three keys, tried IN THIS ORDER: flags || assets || photos. The first present non-empty array is rendered as the gallery; each item follows $defs/galleryItem (each item carries its own source_url + license so attribution survives per asset).

byte_identity.const: verify_map.json must be byte-identical to the inline `verifyMap` <script> island embedded in index.html. The Inspector reads the inline copy at runtime; this file is the on-disk source of truth and the auditable artifact.

decorative_no_entry.const: The five kinds (computation | media | generated | fact | credits) are COMPLETE — there is NO decorative/gradient kind, by design. A purely decorative gradient or scrim is `pointer-events:none`, carries NO data-* token, and therefore has NO verify_map entry at all (validate.py Section 9 also forbids a decorative pointer-events:none element from carrying a data-* token). A CREDITED generated background (an AI atmosphere still that asserts provenance) is NOT decorative: it carries a data-* token and a `kind:"generated"` entry. So: decorative -> no token, no entry; credited generated background -> token + kind:generated.

codeLines.description: Inclusive [start, end] 1-based line span in code_file, or null when the snippet is not a contiguous slice of a single file.

dataPreview.description: A small inlined table sampled from the element's source data, shown in the drawer so a reader sees the actual rows behind a chart/number.

_rows_truncated.description: Optional human note when rows[] is a sample, e.g. 'showing 12 of 30'.

galleryItem.description: One asset in a multi-asset gallery (flags || assets || photos). Each item is self-describing: it carries its own source_url + license so per-asset attribution survives. A filename OR a preview path identifies the asset; a label/team/name/subject names it.

filename.description: Asset path relative to the blog root (e.g. assets/flag_demo.png).

preview.description: Alias for filename when the renderer keys on `preview`.

team.description: Caption when the gallery is a set of national flags.

name.description: Caption when the gallery is a set of named subjects.

source_url.description: Origin URL for THIS asset (per-item attribution).

identity.description: Read-the-file evidence that the asset is what it claims (real photo vs AI, recognisable subject, etc.).

id.description: Optional cross-ref to a scout/source id (e.g. sct_pl_demo).

computation.description: A claim/figure backed by code that produces a number. Renderer shows: claim, the code slice, a data_preview, the expected_output, and a run panel (optionally a client-side reduced-N rerun graded against expected).

claim.description: The published sentence(s) this element substantiates.

cell_id.description: The notebook cell tag (e.g. cell_setup) that re-derives this. Inverse of cell_registry[cell_id].backs.

code_file.description: Repo-relative path to the source script, e.g. code/build_model.py.

code.description: The exact code slice shown in the drawer.

expected_output.description: The literal stdout the code produces, shown so the reader can compare. null when the element has no textual output (e.g. a card grid).

run.description: How (and whether) the element can be re-executed.

type.description: montecarlo = stochastic resample (graded approximately); derived = exact recompute from inlined tables; ratings = network-backed aggregation surfaced read-only.

reduced_n.description: In-browser sample size for a montecarlo rerun (smaller than the published N).

client_model.description: Hook describing the in-page model used for a live reduced-N rerun.

fn.description: Global function the panel calls, e.g. window.DEMO_MODEL.run.

at_rest.description: Where the exact published figures are cached for the static fallback.

methodology.description: Optional path to a longer method writeup.

credits_ref.description: Optional cross-ref to a scout credits id.

photos.description: Optional gallery of subject photos attached to this computation.

media.description: A real (fetched) media asset — image/video/audio. Renderer shows the asset preview plus its source_url, license, author and identity (read-the-file provenance).

preview.description: Asset path, or an array of paths for a multi-asset element.

source_url.description: Origin URL, or an array aligned with preview[].

identity.description: Evidence the asset is what it claims to be (real vs AI, recognisable subject).

embed_url.description: Platform embed URL for media_type audio_embed/video.

generated.description: An AI-generated asset. Renderer shows the generated preview, the full tool/model/prompt, the disclosure label, and a real_default fallback that ships when the AI asset must be swapped at publish.

model.description: Model id used to generate the asset.

purpose.description: Why the asset exists, e.g. IMMERSE.

disclosure.description: On-page disclosure that the asset is AI-generated.

real_default.description: The real asset shown by default (the AI one is opt-in / toggle), so nothing copyrighted or fabricated ships unflagged.

fact.description: A non-computed factual claim grounded in external sources. Renderer shows the claim, its category, and the categorised sources[], each with its own facts[] bullet list.

kind.description: 'fact' = a claim grounded in external sources. 'credits' = the same fact shape used as a license/source aggregator (e.g. a card-deck's data + photo licences); the drawer renders it with a 'Credits' badge instead of 'Fact'.

category.description: Free-form category tag used to colour/group the fact in the drawer (e.g. background, interpretive_hook, controversy, why_it_matters).

facts.description: The specific statements this source supports.

computation_ref.description: Optional cross-ref to a computation id whose number this fact contextualises.

map_markers.description: Optional geo markers when the fact is rendered on a map.
